Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain; [REDACTED]; pain and swelling at the medial aspect of the knee
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. There is a stress fracture of the medial tibial plateau with curvilinear low signal intensity in the subcortical bone measuring up to 1.0 cm anterior posterior by 0.9 cm mediolateral dimension with surrounding marrow edema. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate-to-large joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Minute Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex medial meniscal tears including an oblique component at the posterior horn extending to the free edge. Tears at the undersurface of the body, with subluxation of the body into the medial gutter measuring 2 mm. Subtle high signal intensity at the anterior aspect of the body approximating the superior articular surface.
Medial compartment cartilage: Broad-based area of grade 4 chondrosis along the central the anterior weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle extending over 1.0 cm mediolateral dimension, and up to 1.9 cm anterior posterior dimension. Diffuse thinning of the cartilage of the medial tibial plateau with areas of up to grade 3 chondrosis medially.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Mild intrasubstance heterogeneous signal intensity in the body without definite tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Scattered areas of up to grade 2/3 chondrosis at the medial patellar facet measuring up to 0.5 cm mediolateral dimension. Grade 2/3 chondrosis in the medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact with mild subsidence heterogeneous signal intensity.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Mild to moderate sprain of the medial collateral ligament with focal thickening and heterogeneous signal intensity at the proximal fibers, and edema surrounding the mid to distal fibers.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Edema in the popliteus muscle belly. Otherwise unremarkable.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Attenuation of the posterior fibers with surrounding soft tissue swelling.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Mild lateral patellar tilt without translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Edema is noted in the popliteus muscle. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Significant abnormality: This examination demonstrates an abnormality/anomaly that warrants follow-up or additional medical care within 3 months. [REDACTED]. (96)

IMPRESSION:

1. Stress fracture of the medial tibial plateau measuring approximately 0.9 x 1.0 cm with surrounding marrow edema.

2. Complex medial meniscal tears of the posterior horn and body with inferior and medial subluxation of the body into the medial gutter.

3. Mild to moderate sprain of the medial collateral ligament with surrounding edema.

4. Moderate to advanced medial compartment osteoarthritis with areas of to grade 4 chondrosis in the medial femoral condyle.

5. Moderate patellofemoral osteoarthritis with areas of grade 2/3 chondrosis.

6. Moderate to large joint effusion.

COMMUNICATION FOLLOW-UP: Documentation of communications managed and recorded in Si.

Right knee MRI:

Indication: Right knee swelling rule out internal derangement.

COMPARISON: Compare with bilateral knee radiograph from [Date].

FINDINGS:

Large knee effusion with extensive synovitis. No significant Baker's cyst. There is thickening of the medial and lateral plica.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Severe chondrosis involving the femoral patellar compartment with complete delamination of the lateral facet of the patella and subchondral edema. There is area of full-thickness fissuring and significant thinning of the lateral trochlear surface. Chondrosis is milder on the medial facet of the patella. Lateral subluxation of the patella in regards to the trochlea.
Extensor mechanism appears unremarkable. Hoffa's fat pad unremarkable.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Moderate severe chondrosis with area of full-thickness cartilage delamination without subchondral edema or cyst. Intermediate signal within the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with maceration. No discrete tear. Small meniscal flounce at the anterior body.
Medial collateral ligament intact. Portions visualize of the pes anserine unremarkable. Mild semimembranosus tendinosis.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT :
Mild chondrosis. No discrete meniscal tear. Popliteus tendon lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris unremarkable. Proximal tibiofibular joint unremarkable. Iliotibial band unremarkable.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament intact. Small intercondylar notch ganglion cysts measuring 1.5 x 1.4 x 2.4 cm.

Main neurovascular structures reveal visualized are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:
1. Severe osteoarthritis involving the femoropatellar compartment and moderate to severe osteoarthritis to the medial compartment and milder chondrosis to the lateral compartment.

2. Large effusions with extensive synovitis associated. Considering the extent of the synovitis could inflammatory arthritis be associated? Although the OA as a more mechanical distribution.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION: Left knee injury [Date] with persistent pain on flexion. Ultrasound showed severely thickened and hypoechoic posterior cruciate ligament (report attached)/ ? PCL strain/tear

PRIOR IMAGING: None available at our institution.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The quadriceps tendon is intact. The patellar tendon is intact.

Articular irregularity and signal heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage, and underlying marrow edema overall suggestive of severe chondromalacia patellae.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. The tibial aspect of the posterior cruciate ligament is relatively thickened with focal intermediate signal thickening suggestive of scar tissue, and suggestive of previously low-grade partial tear. No posterior tibial translation.

The anterior horn medial meniscus is slightly extruded 3 mm beyond the tibial plateau. No medial meniscal tear is identified. Mild chondrosis medial tibiofemoral compartment.

The lateral meniscus is intact without evidence of tear. Mild chondrosis lateral tibiofemoral compartment.

No significant knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone contusion anterior tibia, just lateral to the tibial tubercle. Mild prepatellar soft tissue swelling.

INTERPRETATION: 

- Findings suggestive of previous posterior cruciate ligament low-grade partial tear. No abnormal tibial translation.
- Severe chondromalacia patellae. Mild chondrosis within the medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartments.
- Bone contusion anterior tibia just lateral to the tibial tubercle.

No significant knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is moderate patellofemoral dysplasia but normal alignment of the patella. T T T G distance is widened and measures 25 mm.  Normal tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues. A collapsed Baker's cyst is noted.  Conclusion: No meniscal tear. No significant Baker's cyst formation. Patellofemoral dysplasia but no evidence of patellofemoral degeneration.

Findings:  No significant knee effusion. A small free edge radial tear of the body of lateral meniscus is noted. Normal medial meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild generalized thinning of the tibiofemoral compartment articular cartilage. Focal fraying of the medial patellar facet articular cartilage is noted with mild underlying bony change. Normal trochlear articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: Small free edge radial tear of the lateral meniscus. No medial meniscal tear. Mild tibiofemoral and patellar chondral the as described.

There is a minor knee effusion. The posterior medial meniscus is attenuated in size. No definite tear is identified. A tiny free edge radial tear is noted in the posterior body of the lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is well preserved. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.
